summary.headline: Bajaj Consumer Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% to INR341 crore, with EBITDA margin at 24.7% despite gross margin falling to 61.8%.
summary.overview: Revenue was INR341 crore, up over 28% YoY, with consolidated EBITDA of INR84.4 crore (24.7% margin, roughly doubled) and PAT of INR70.7 crore (20.7% margin). Gross margin fell sequentially from 63% to 61.8% due to West Asia-driven raw material and packaging inflation, partly offset by selective price increases and MLH (mass-level hike/reduction) changes. Fixed costs including employee and other costs were held down, creating operating leverage, while advertising was kept at 14.6% of revenue. Management guided that Q2 gross margin will be under more stress than Q1, with easing expected in Q3 and Q4, and said pricing will not drive further margin expansion.

segments.name: Almond Drop Hair Oil (ADHO)
segments.commentary: Low-teens volume growth on an MLH-adjusted basis, driven by small packs and sachets across all pack groups and channels; approx. 80% of revenue. Influencer-led digital marketing was increased.

segments.name: Growth portfolio (non-ADHO, incl. coconut and Banjara's)
segments.commentary: Grew high single-digit QoQ; coconut volumes rose sequentially despite a value correction, with the company saying it reduced the discount to the market leader. Management aspires to grow this portfolio in the high 20s long term.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Strong rebound on a weak base: Nepal and Bangladesh grew double digits with margin improvement; MENA and rest of world also rebounded strongly.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: General trade grew in line with organized trade, both in the 20s%; modern trade and e-commerce performed well. Institutional business was weak but is under 1% of mix.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected to stay under tougher pressure in Q2 FY27 than Q1, then ease sequentially over Q3 and Q4.
Management reiterated an aspiration to operate in the low-to-mid 20s EBITDA margin; it does not give formal quarterly or annual guidance.
Pricing is not expected to drive further margin expansion; no pricing actions are currently planned.
Long-term aspiration of consistent double-digit to low-teens revenue growth; management said it would be disappointed by anything below double digits.
Advertising to stay in the historical 15-16% of revenue range over the medium term.
Aarohan distribution initiative adds a one-time 200-300 bps benefit in newly executed states, with multi-year benefit after.
capex_capacity: Project Aarohan (direct distribution expansion) executed for the first time in four large states this quarter; expected to be a multi-year exercise.
No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed in the call.
demand_pricing: Selective and calibrated price increases plus MLH reduction across the portfolio to offset input inflation from the West Asia war.
Petroleum-linked inputs (LLP, packaging) and edible oils (mustard, almond) remain inflated; high-cost inventory is still in the system.
Copra has deflated from historic highs to roughly 130-140 per the management in recent months, but the outlook is volatile and is managed month-on-month.
ADHO volume growth accelerated to low teens from mid-single digits in prior quarters, driven by smaller unit price points.
Coconut volume growth came from distribution and wider availability, not free volumes; coconut faces a very competitive market.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-off in Q1 margins, given muted other expenses, and should margins be expected to moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no significant one-offs, only timing variations in expenses. Gross margin will stay tough in Q2 and ease in Q3-Q4; pricing will not drive further expansion; EBITDA depends on revenue flow-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still at a 20%+ margin, given the lower-end guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is happy operating in the low-to-mid 20s EBITDA margin range, with quarters varying between the lower and higher ends. It does not give specific guidance, and any cost skew between quarters is natural, not deferral.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the growth is from Aarohan versus non-Aarohan states?
qa_highlights.answer: Aarohan gives a one-time 200-300 bps delta on first execution because of channel mix change, with ongoing efficiency gains. Management said it is difficult to separate the effect from other drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is coconut volume growth driven by grammage increases or free volume?
qa_highlights.answer: No substantial free volume is being given; the growth comes from distribution and wider availability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term growth aspiration given Q1 growth of 28%?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been exponential on a weak base; the aspiration is consistent double-digit growth, and management will not give quarterly guidance. The growth portfolio aspiration is high 20s long term.

qa_highlights.question: What are Banjara's contribution and M&A plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Banjara's is about 5% of revenue, with revamp and pilots under way; disclosure will come annually. No M&A updates to disclose.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure in Q2 FY27 from high-cost inventory and volatile petroleum and edible oil prices; a further change in the West Asia war outlook could alter this.
Sustainability of the 28% growth as the company laps its exceptional base from the past four quarters.
Execution risk in gaining market share, which management identifies as the largest risk to sustaining growth.
Coconut and growth-portfolio competitive intensity and limited disclosure; Banjara's still early-stage.
Sequential easing of spot prices expected over the next few months but the outlook is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and brand momentum, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly said Q2 gross margin will be under more stress and declined to give specific guidance or quantify the outlook beyond the directional aspiration.
key_quotes: While from a supply chain perspective, we believe the worst is behind us, we do have high-cost inventory in our system and the spot prices are also expected to cool sequentially over the next few months.
